rejected_attempt.reason: Shared template publication reduced publication stage cost but regressed native asynchronous cadence by 24.2% and worsened lag/RSS. All publication changes from this iteration were withdrawn; receipts preserved.

validation.postgres: Separate fresh databases bot_commit_rust_1012 and bot_commit_http_1012 at localhost:56681; fsync, synchronous_commit and full_page_writes on; task cluster stopped afterward.
validation.environment_receipt: Initial PowerShell pg_ctl output pipe remained open after launcher exit. Retried using a hidden detached launcher and separate process wait; initial database creation failure occurred before Rust tests, and is retained in validation-run.log. No database/recovery safety checks were relaxed.

limitations: Short memory-journal load windows, not PostgreSQL capacity or long-run qualification.
ABBA uses two runs per version; asynchronous trades can differ, so cadence alone is not fixed transaction throughput.
Only the three bundled MA/RSI/breakout sources use the opt-in Rust route in the load test. Default Python-worker throughput and arbitrary Pine sources are unqualified.
Successful commit-return is a batch-return latency proxy, not proof of each intent admission or bar-close-to-durable-order latency.
Encoding cache benchmark is isolated fixed work; do not convert its speedup into bot capacity.
History/state bounds, journal schema and cadence, full retained transcripts, risk/gateway checks and source qualification remain unchanged.
